passages.scripture: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings.

lines.text: James writes this letter.
James serves God.
James serves the Lord Jesus Christ.
James writes to the twelve tribes.
These twelve tribes live in the Dispersion.
James greets these twelve tribes.

passages.scripture: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.

lines.text: You will face many kinds of trials.
When you face these trials, consider it pure joy.
You know that these trials test your faith.
The testing of your faith produces perseverance.

passages.scripture: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.

lines.text: Perseverance must finish its work.
This work is important.
It helps you become mature.
It helps you become complete.
You will not lack anything if perseverance finishes its work.

passages.scripture: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.

lines.text: If any of you lacks wisdom, ask God for it.
God gives wisdom to everyone generously.
God does not find fault when you ask.
God will give wisdom to the one who asks.

passages.scripture: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

lines.text: A person should ask God for wisdom.
He must ask with faith.
He must not doubt.
A person who doubts is like a wave in the sea.
The wind blows and tosses the wave.
Doubt makes a person unstable, like that wave.

passages.scripture: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.

lines.text: A man who doubts should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.
God may not give to those who do not ask in faith.
A doubting person may not receive from God.

passages.scripture: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

lines.text: A double-minded man doubts.
He is unstable in all his ways.
He does not stand firm in anything he does.

passages.scripture: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.

lines.text: A Christian brother may live in humble circumstances.
He may be poor or lowly.
He should rejoice.
God gives him a high position in the kingdom of God.
God honors those who are humble.

passages.scripture: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.

lines.text: A rich person should rejoice in being made low.
He will not remain great on earth forever.
He will pass away.
He will fade like a flower in a field.

passages.scripture: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.

lines.text: The sun rises.
The sun brings scorching heat.
The heat withers the plant.
The flower of the plant falls.
The beauty of the flower is lost.
In the same way, the rich man will fade away.
He will fade away while he goes about his pursuits.

passages.scripture: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him.

lines.text: God promises a reward to those who love Him.
This reward includes the crown of life.
A man who perseveres under trial is blessed.
This man stands firm when he faces testing.
After he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life.

passages.scripture: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.

lines.text: God is holy.
God cannot be tempted by evil.
God does not tempt anyone.
If you are tempted, do not say, "God is tempting me."

passages.scripture: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.

lines.text: Each person faces temptation.
Evil desires inside each person cause this temptation.
These desires pull the person away from what is right.
These desires attract and entice the person.

passages.scripture: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.

lines.text: Desire comes from within a person.
Desire grows inside the person.
Desire produces sin.
Sin grows and becomes complete.
Sin produces death.

passages.scripture: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.

lines.text: James writes to his beloved brothers.
James says, "Do not be deceived."

passages.scripture: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.

lines.text: God is the Father of the heavenly lights.
He gives every good gift.
He gives every perfect gift.
These gifts come from above.
God sends these gifts down to us.
God never changes.
God does not shift like a shadow.
God is always the same.

passages.scripture: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation.

lines.text: God is the Father of the heavenly lights.
God does not change.
God chose to give us new birth.
God used the word of truth to give us this new birth.
God made us a kind of firstfruits of His creation.

passages.scripture: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger, for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.

lines.text: James writes to Christians.
He calls them his beloved brothers.
He gives them a command.
He says, "Understand this."
Every person should be quick to listen.
Every person should be slow to speak.
Every person should be slow to become angry.
Human anger does not produce the righteousness that God wants.

passages.scripture: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.

lines.text: God wants you to live in a way that pleases Him.
You must remove all moral filth from your life.
You must get rid of every kind of evil.
You must accept the word God has planted in you.
You must accept this word with humility.
This word can save your soul.

passages.scripture: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.

lines.text: Be doers of the word.
Do not be hearers only.
If you only listen and do not obey the word, you deceive yourselves.

passages.scripture: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror, and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.

lines.text: Anyone who hears the word but does not do what it says is like a man.
This man looks at his own face in a mirror.
He sees himself.
He goes away.
He immediately forgets what he looks like.

passages.scripture: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so—not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer—he will be blessed in what he does.

lines.text: A person looks carefully into the perfect law.
This law gives freedom.
He keeps looking into this law.
He does not forget what he hears.
He does what the law says.
This person does good works.
God will bless him in what he does.

passages.scripture: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.

lines.text: A person may think he is religious.
Yet, he does not control his tongue.
This man deceives his own heart.
His religion is worthless.

passages.scripture: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.

lines.text: God is our Father.
Visit orphans when they are in trouble.
Visit widows when they are in trouble.
Keep yourself clean from the world.
Do not let the world pollute you.
God sees all this as pure and undefiled religion.
